title: AO/709/2017 of Vishu Bhatia AND ANOTHER Vs M/s Dreamers Magic Llp

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Appeal from Order No. 709 of 2017
Vishu Bhatia & Another ..Defendants/Appellants

Versus
M/s Dreamers Magic LLP ...Plaintiff/Respondent
With
Appeal from Order No. 710 of 2017
Vishu Bhatia & Another ..Defendants/Appellants

Versus
M/s Dreamers Magic LLP ...Plaintiff/Respondent
Present: Mr. Neeraj Garg, Advocate for the defendants/appellants
Mr. Sandeep Kothari, Advocate for the respondent
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J. (Oral)
 A very perplexed situation which has arisen in this
Appeal from Order, the facts are that the
defendant(s)/appellant(s) of Suit No. 31 of 2017 "M/s
Dreamers Magic LLP Vs. Vishu Bhatia & another", was
preferred by the plaintiff/respondent, questioning the
validity of the order dated 30.11.2017, granting injunction
in favour of the plaintiff/respondent against which the
defendant(s)/appellant(s) has preferred the present Appeal
from Order being A.O. No. 709 of 2017.

2
2. The brief line of arguments of the learned counsel for
the defendant(s)/appellant(s) is that the appellants claims
themselves to be the owner of the resort, for which,
exclusively its management and upkeep he has executed
a registered agreement on 05.07.2014 in favour of the
plaintiff/respondent, an inter-se relationship arising of this
agreement of agency between the plaintiff and the
defendant was to be governed strictly in terms of the
agreement dated 05.07.2014.
3. The Suit which the respondent preferred, he has
sought a decree by way of permanent injunction, seeking a
restraint order against the defendant from interfering into
day-to-day affairs of the resort functioning in the name and
style of "Surabhi Hotel".
4. The contention of the learned counsel for the
appellants is that the application for grant of injunction
during the pendency of the Suit No. 31 of 2017 "M/s
Dreamers Magic LLP Vs. Vishu Bhatia & another" was to
the following effect:-

5. What he tries to submit is if the prayer of the
Injunction Application is taken into consideration vis-à-vis
the relief granted by the impugned order, it happens to be
beyond the relief sought for by the plaintiff in the
application under Order 39 Rule 1 & 2, because in the
concluding part of the operative portion of the order,
learned Civil Judge (Sr. Div.), Tehri Garhwal has directed
the compliance of the agreement dated 05.07.2014, which
was not a relief claimed in the application for temporary
injunction.
6. The defendant(s) in the Suit No. 31 of 2017 "M/s
Dreamers Magic LLP Vs. Vishu Bhatia & another" has also
filed a counterclaim, invoking Order 8 Rule 6A, wherein he
has sought the relief for declaration of the agreement
dated 05.07.2014 to be void, as having been obtained by
fraud. His counterclaim too accompanied with an
application for the grant of temporary injunction, in which
the defendant(s) has sought the following relief :-

7. The relief as claimed for by the
defendant(s)/appellant(s) for injunction has been rejected
by the learned Civil Judge (Sr. Div.), Tehri Garhwal by its
impugned order dated 30.11.2017 on the ground that as
per the agreement, he is not in possession, the said order

4
of rejection of temporary injunction in counterclaim, has
been put to challenge in the Appeal from Order No. 710 of
2017 "Vishu Bhatia & another Vs. M/s Dreamers Magic
LLP."
8. In these circumstances, the prayer which has been
sought for by the defendant(s) is to the effect that the
consequential affect of the impugned order under
challenge before this Court by virtue of the present Appeal
from Order has arisen is that despite of the fact that he
being the owner of the property, he is not even been
permitted to enter into his own premises which he owns,
though it was one of the convonent of the agreement
dated 05.07.2014, which entitled him to enter into his
premises without any restrictions. But since the veracity of
the agreement itself has been questioned by the
defendant(s)/appellant(s) by filing a counterclaim, which is
sub-judice, coupled with the fact that he has questioned
part of the findings recorded in the impugned order under
challenge in the A.O. No. 710 of 2017, so far it relates to
the direction to enforce the agreement dated 05.07.2014,
he simultaneously cannot enforce part of the order for
getting the interim relief to the effect that he may be
permitted to enter into the premises on the basis of the
conditions covered by the agreement dated 05.07.2014.
Because even otherwise also, in case if the relief prayed
for by the appellant(s) is granted at this stage, this Court is
of a considered opinion that it would rather multiply the
intricacies of the disputes, rather than resolving it, because

5
by a permission of entrance into the premises it may
further would also lead to an interference in the affairs
which so far is claimed by the plaintiff that he is managing
it under the agreement.
9. Owning to the above circumstances, in all fitness of
things, this Court feels that the affairs of the resort would
temporarily continued to be maintained by the
plaintiff/respondent within the scope of the agreement itself
(this will not amount to either acceptance or denial of the
agreement dated 05.07.2014 by this Court), with a rider
that plaintiff not to undertake any material alterations or
changes or create any encumbrance of any nature during
the pendency of the Suit. Learned Civil Judge (Sr. Div.),
Tehri Garhwal, New Tehri is requested to decide the Suit
itself expeditiously, but under no circumstances beyond
the period of one year without granting unnecessary
adjournments to either of the parties.
10. Subject to the above observations, the Appeals are
disposed of. No order as to costs.
